newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SKIFLYING-PETERKA WINS WORLD CUP EVENT.
newsitem.headline: SKIFLYING-PETERKA WINS WORLD CUP EVENT.

text.p: Slovenia's Primoz Peterka won a World Cup ski-flying competition on Sunday and strengthened his lead in the world standings over Germany's Dieter Thoma.

The 17-year old Peterka, making his debut on the world's largest natural ski jump, the Kulm, had jumps of 195.5 and 203.5 metres to push local favourite Andreas Goldberger into second place for the second day.
Japan's Takanobu Okabe, who won on Saturday and smashed the Kulm's record with a leap of 205 metres in training, was let down by a short second jump and finished third.

Peterka's victory in front of 40,000 raucous spectators takes his tally to six World Cup wins and widens his advantage over Thoma, who decided against competing on the Kulm to prepare for the world championships in Trondheim next week.
Peterka heads the world standings with 1,097 points, Thoma follows 13 points behind, and Austria's Goldberger, who became world champion last year on the Kulm, lags behind with 817.
